SE will run a 10k prompt benchmark and report latency/cost. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs and canary timeline. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-25 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (NexaHealth CTO), Daniel Kim (Staff ML Eng), Lina Gomez (Security Ops)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check in — can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Priya Patel: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Awesome. High level agenda, want to cover onboarding progress, access setup (VPC, service account), run through security docs, and then Carlos will talk about the benchmark plan.
[00:24] Daniel Kim: Sounds good — we made some progress on IAM but still need peering, we hit a snag with our infra team needing details on routes.
[00:32] Carlos Rivera: Ok noted. For the peering we only need one route and the CIDR ranges, and a service account with KMS decrypt so we can pull the test keys, nothing more than least privilege.
[00:42] Lina Gomez: Quick security question — you mentioned KMS/HSM access earlier, is that managed by Redwood or do we use our own KMS?
[00:48] Maya Chen: Good call. For Private deployments the customer can bring their own KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles. I'll attach the KMS integration doc after the call.
[00:59] Priya Patel: Ok, would you also share SOC2 and the security questionnaire we filled out last week?
[01:04] Maya Chen: Yep I'll send the SOC2 link plus the updated questionnaire; updated security answers included.
[01:10] Daniel Kim: On the benchmark, our main success criteria are p50 latency under 300ms for short prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under our target. We'll also check hallucination regression on the evaluation set.
[01:21] Carlos Rivera: Great — our plan is to run two runs: hosted baseline on Redwood Hosted API, then private/dedicated variant with quantized model. We'll record throughput, p50/p95, token cost, and quality metrics on the eval set.
[01:34] Priya Patel: Is the quantization going to affect quality much? We want to avoid regressing on medical QA.
[01:40] Carlos Rivera: Good question. We'll include mixed-precision and 4-bit q configs; typically we see small diff on targeted evals but we'll measure BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and also do manual spot checks on medical prompts.
[01:50] Daniel Kim: Please note we need chain-of-custody for data and logs — audit logs need to be exportable to our SIEM.
[01:57] Maya Chen: Redwood Console exposes audit logs and we can push to your endpoints — I'll have the integration steps in the security doc.
[02:05] Lina Gomez: Are there any compliance blockers for on-prem/private? We have some regulated data that can't leave region.
[02:12] Carlos Rivera: We support region pinning for Private deployments; if on-prem is required we can run air-gapped build with HSM and local KMS. That usually adds a bit of ops time but it's doable.
[02:23] Priya Patel: Ops time meaning weeks? We need a pilot timeline.
[02:27] Maya Chen: For a private canary it's typically 2-4 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM onboarding. For Dedicated in a cloud region it's closer to 1-2 weeks.
[02:35] Daniel Kim: Ok we'll try to get peering fast then so we can do Dedicated first as a low-friction path.
[02:40] Maya Chen: Good plan. Carlos, could you walk through the benchmark steps and what you need from Nexa?
[02:45] Carlos Rivera: Sure. Step 1: we need a sample eval set (we recommend 10k prompts with anonymized medical-style questions). Step 2: permissions — service account with IAM for VPC peering and KMS decrypt for test keys. Step 3: target configs — sequence lengths, model variant preferences (we'll run rdx-3b and rdx-7b quantized variants). Step 4: run hosted vs dedicated and gather latency/cost/quality.
[03:08] Daniel Kim: We can provide the eval set, but will anonymize and strip PHI.
[03:12] Carlos Rivera: Perfect, that'll help. Also I'll include a cost spreadsheet showing tokens, inference cost, and estimated monthly extrapolation.
[03:18] Priya Patel: On the legal side, I'm trying to gauge procurement timeline. Lina, any blockers from security right now?
[03:24] Lina Gomez: Need to review SOC2 and encryption at rest details. Also confirm we can keep audit logs for 1 year.
[03:30] Maya Chen: We can support 1yr retention for audit logs as an add-on; I'll include the options/pricing.
[03:36] Priya Patel: Great. A small note — earlier when you guys demoed the Console, we saw token-level cost breakdown, can we get a sample report?
[03:44] Carlos Rivera: Yes I'll attach a sample Console export and the tracing hooks doc. There's also a CSV export for token-level billing.
[03:50] Daniel Kim: About canary — if we do a small canary in our dev VPC, what's the rollback story if latency jumps?
[03:56] Carlos Rivera: Canary uses routing policies: we can split traffic and fallback to a hosted model if latency exceeds thresholds. We also set automatic canary health checks and alerts.
[04:06] Priya Patel: That helps. One more technical: you mentioned KV cache earlier — how does that work across instances?
[04:11] Carlos Rivera: KV cache is localized per serving node but we have prefix caching strategies that keep hot prefixes in memory; for Dedicated we can pin customer-specific cache shards. Apologies if earlier notes said K V cash...
[04:22] Maya Chen: (laughs) transcription aside, good detail.
[04:26] Lina Gomez: For encryption key management, what permissions does your service account need?
[04:31] Carlos Rivera: Minimal KMS decrypt and the ability to fetch model artifacts if in private mode. For cloud-managed KMS we use short-lived keys and audit every access.
[04:40] Priya Patel: Ok. Timeline check — if Daniel provisions peering and service account by Friday, when can Carlos run the benchmark?
[04:47] Carlos Rivera: I can start the harness within 24 hours of access; full runs and analysis should be ready in 4 business days.
[04:53] Daniel Kim: We'll aim to have access by 2027-08-27 EOD.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Great. Quick recap of action items then...
[05:01] Maya Chen: I'll send SOC2 + security questionnaire, sample Console export, and the KMS integration doc tomorrow. Carlos will run the 10k prompt benchmark after access and send results. Daniel will provision peering and service account. Priya will confirm procurement timeline.
[05:18] Priya Patel: That sounds right. Any other blockers?
[05:22] Lina Gomez: No, just want the SOC2 before security signs off.
[05:25] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize that. Thanks everyone for the time. We'll follow up in Slack and set next sync for next Tuesday same time unless you prefer different cadence.
[05:35] Daniel Kim: Next Tuesday works. Thanks.
[05:38] Maya Chen: Thanks all, bye.

Notes: transcript has minor transcription errors and occasional speaker label issues, and timestamps are approximate. Attachments referenced: SOC2 link, security-questionnaire.pdf, console-export-sample.csv, kms-integration.md, benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx
